name: WPI FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Applications typically open mid-December and close in late February
notes: For FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, or FIRST Global Challenge team members admitted to WPI. One of the largest scholarships available to FIRST alumni.

name: Rose-Hulman FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Typically due February 1 — must already be admitted to apply
notes: Two awarded per year to admitted students who competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition team, contingent on maintaining good academic standing.

name: Kettering University Robotics Scholarship
amount: Up to $5,000/year, up to $25,000 over 5 years
notes: Awarded annually to FRC/VEX competitors — 88 scholarships were awarded in 2025 alone.

name: Michigan Tech FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Open to incoming students who competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, or VEX Robotics team. Not automatic with admission — a separate application is required.

name: FIRST Scholarship Program
deadline: Check current cycle on Detroit Mercy's site
notes: For high school seniors with a background in robotics, including FIRST Robotics Competition participants.

name: FIRST Scholars Award
deadline: Check current cycle on Mercer's site
notes: Awarded to admitted students selected as Mercer FIRST Scholars based on their FIRST program participation.

name: FIRST/VEX Robotics Engineering Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on Oregon Tech's site
notes: Two awarded per year. Requires two years of active participation and demonstrated leadership on a FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, or VEX team.

name: FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Georgia Tech application plus FAFSA and CSS Profile, all due January 31
notes: Need-based award offered to graduating high school seniors admitted to Georgia Tech who participated in FIRST Robotics Competition.

name: Elbit America FIRST Robotics Scholarship (New Hampshire)
deadline: Check current cycle on Elbit America's application portal
notes: Restricted to New Hampshire high school seniors who competed on a FIRST Robotics Competition team.

name: Stamps President's Scholars Program
amount: Full ride — tuition, fees, room & board, books, and personal expenses for up to 4 years
deadline: Tied to Georgia Tech's Early Action admission deadline; semifinalists notified in January, finalists invited to Scholars Weekend in late February
notes: Open to US and UK high school seniors applying for admission to Georgia Tech. About 50 awarded per year through a multi-round process including a semifinalist interview and a finalist weekend; no separate application beyond Georgia Tech admission.

name: Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship
amount: $2,500/year honorary award for scholars without demonstrated need; scholars with need receive funding up to their full calculated need
deadline: No separate application — tied to the UC application (due in November); interviews in early March, decisions by late March
notes: Awarded to incoming first-years and some transfers based on academic achievement, leadership, and service shown on the UC application; renewable for up to 8 semesters.

name: Engineering Scholarship of Honor
provider: University of Michigan College of Engineering
amount: $10,000/year for in-state students; $10,000–$30,000/year for out-of-state students, renewable up to 8 semesters
deadline: No separate application — automatic consideration upon admission, with award notification typically by mid-April
notes: All admitted US citizens and permanent residents entering the College of Engineering are automatically considered based on their admissions application.

name: Trustees Scholarship
amount: $10,000/year for Indiana residents; $16,000/year for non-residents, renewable up to 4 years with a 3.00 Purdue GPA
deadline: November 1 — no separate application; automatic merit review of the admission application
notes: Awarded to incoming first-year applicants for exceptional academic achievement plus leadership or service in school or community.

name: President's Endowed Scholarship
amount: $3,000/year for 4 years ($12,000 total), plus a one-time $1,000 study-abroad award; renewable with a 3.5 cumulative GPA
deadline: December 1 — covered by the same admission/scholarship application (ApplyTexas or Common App)
notes: Merit-based award for entering first-time freshmen in the top 25% of their graduating class; no separate scholarship application required.

name: Barry M. Goldwater Scholarship
deadline: National deadline is the last Friday in January; each college sets its own earlier internal nomination deadline, often November–December
notes: For current college sophomores and juniors (3.0+ GPA, US citizen, national, or permanent resident) pursuing a research career in natural sciences, mathematics, or engineering. Requires nomination by your institution — students cannot apply directly.

name: SWE Scholarship Program
amount: Individual awards generally $1,000–$10,000, varying by named award within the program
deadline: Varies by track — Collegiate/Graduate Scholars and Emerging First-Year Scholars tracks typically close in late winter/early spring
notes: Open to women entering or enrolled in an ABET-accredited undergraduate or graduate engineering, engineering technology, or computer science program. One application considers a student for all eligible society-level awards.

name: NSBE Scholarships
deadline: Varies by cycle — multiple cycles run per year; check current dates on NSBE's site
notes: Requires active, paid NSBE membership and a verified GPA on file. Specific major, classification, and residency requirements vary by individual sponsored award.

name: AISES Scholarships
provider: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
deadline: Applications generally open mid-December and close April 30 each cycle
notes: Requires free AISES student membership and full-time enrollment in a STEM field at an accredited institution. A single profile in AISES's OASIS portal matches students to eligible named scholarships.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
amount: Top 300 scholars each receive $2,000 (plus $2,000 to their school); 40 finalists receive at least $25,000, with top awards up to $250,000
deadline: Early November — check current cycle on site
notes: Open to students in their final year of secondary school in the US or its territories, including US citizens studying abroad, based on an original, independent research project. Team research is not eligible.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
deadline: Mid-February — check current cycle on site
notes: Open to students 18 or younger who have completed a significant, original piece of work in STEM, technology, engineering, math, or other fields. Individuals or 2-person teams are eligible. The top $100,000 tier is open to all categories, not just STEM/math.

name: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
notes: Not FIRST-exclusive, but manufacturing/engineering-focused scholarships that many FRC alumni are well-positioned for given hands-on robotics experience.

name: NFPA Robotics Challenge Scholarship
amount: $30,000 total ($7,500/year for 4 years), one merit-based award
deadline: Check current cycle on NFPA's site
notes: For a high school senior who participated in FIRST Robotics Competition or the National Robotics League. The team's competition robot must have used pneumatics — a mentor letter confirming this is required.

name: TMC SAE Donald D. Dawson Technical Scholarship
amount: $1,500/year, renewable up to 3 years (~$4,500 total per secondary sources; not confirmed on the official page)
notes: For students pursuing an engineering or related science degree through an ABET-accredited program who can show hands-on technical experience — SAE explicitly lists FIRST or VEX robotics competition participation as qualifying activity alongside things like engine work or coding projects.

name: IEEE Presidents' Scholarship
amount: $10,000 (1st place, payable over 4 years); 2nd/3rd place amounts could not be verified — official page would not load
deadline: No separate application — awarded to finalists at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF), typically held in May
notes: Recognizes an outstanding ISEF finalist project in electrical engineering, electronics, computer science, or another IEEE field — robotics and automation builds are a recurring winning project category. Students qualify by reaching ISEF with their project, not by a direct application.

name: ScholarSHPE
amount: Individual awards vary; SHPE distributes over $1 million annually across its scholarship portfolio
deadline: Typically opens early February and closes mid-February for the main cycle; check current dates on SHPE's site
notes: Requires active SHPE membership (free/low-cost to join) and enrollment in a STEM degree program; one common application considers students for all eligible named awards. SHPE chapters frequently mentor and sponsor FIRST/VEX robotics teams, so robotics experience is a strong fit for applicant essays.

name: ASME INSPIRE/Charles W.E. Clarke Scholarship
notes: For graduating high school seniors planning to enroll in an ABET-accredited mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology program. ASME is a longtime FIRST Robotics sponsor and judge partner, and reviewers favor applicants who can point to hands-on project experience like robotics build season.

name: Astronaut Scholarship
deadline: Nomination-only — partner-university liaisons submit nominations by late March each year
notes: Awarded to STEM sophomores/juniors doing hands-on research or engineering work, through faculty nomination at ~45 partner universities only (no direct student application). FRC alumni heading into autonomous systems, aerospace, or robotics research are well-positioned if their university is a partner — ask an engineering advisor about nomination early in the fall term.

name: William P. Elrod Memorial Scholarship
notes: For a TSA student member pursuing a STEM path. TSA's national competitive events include a Robotics and Automation category, and many FRC/VEX competitors already hold TSA membership through their school's CTE or STEM program.

name: Adrian College FIRST Robotics Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Ten awarded to incoming students who competed in FRC or FTC. Minimum 3.0 GPA.

name: Bob Bonczyk Memorial Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Awarded each year to a graduating senior showing commitment to robotics, team leadership, and community impact. Appears tied to Team 107's program in Michigan, so check eligibility on the team's page.

name: Cirkled In "No Sweat" Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Not FIRST-exclusive: open to all U.S. high school students in grades 9-12. No essay, minimum GPA, or recommendation letters.

name: Drexel FIRST Robotics Scholarship
deadline: February 1, 2027 for Regular Decision; November 25 for Early Decision and Early Action
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For FIRST Robotics team members. Requires a supplemental application in Discover Drexel.

name: Embry-Riddle FIRST Scholarship (Daytona Beach)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For select FRC and FTC participants. Reviewed on academics, leadership, community service, and an essay.

name: Florida Tech FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For applying first-year students who are currently part of FIRST.

name: Hanover College FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For FRC or FTC participants. Requires the FIRST Scholarship form and a letter from a FIRST mentor or coach. Must be admitted to be selected.

name: Indiana Tech FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For FIRST participants entering the Talwar College of Engineering and Computer Sciences on the Fort Wayne campus.

name: Luddy FIRST Robotics Scholarship
provider: Indiana University Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering
amount: Up to $2,000/year for up to 4 years
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For incoming IU Bloomington students who took part in FRC or FTC and are pursuing a Luddy undergraduate degree.

name: Kansas State Engineering FIRST Scholarship
provider: Kansas State University Carl R. Ice College of Engineering
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For first-year engineering students.

name: Lawrence Tech FIRST Robotics Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For newly admitted first-year FIRST team members with at least a 3.0 GPA. Requires a 500-word essay and a mentor recommendation.

name: Merrimack College FIRST Robotics Scholarship
amount: $5,000, renewable up to $20,000 over 4 years (up to ten awarded)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For high school seniors who took part in FIRST and will study a STEM field at Merrimack.

name: Miami University FIRST Scholarship
provider: Miami University College of Engineering and Computing
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For an incoming engineering or computing major who took part in FIRST Robotics. Minimum 3.0 GPA.

name: Missouri S&T FIRST Robotics Scholarship
provider: Missouri University of Science and Technology
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Competitive award for incoming full-time freshmen who were on a FIRST Robotics team in high school.

name: Tahnoon bin Zayed Scholarship in AI Excellence
provider: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)
amount: $45,000 on the portal; may cover up to 100% of tuition
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Not FIRST-exclusive: merit-based, for students in MBZUAI's BS in Artificial Intelligence in Abu Dhabi, UAE. Open to UAE nationals and international students.

name: NYU Tandon FIRST Scholarship
provider: New York University Tandon School of Engineering
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For high school students who are or were on an FRC or FTC team. Requires a brief application and a recommendation letter.

name: Olin College FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For full-time entering freshmen who were on a FIRST team in high school.

name: Kansas State Project Lead The Way Scholarship
provider: Kansas State University Carl R. Ice College of Engineering
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Tied to Project Lead The Way rather than FIRST. For first-year engineering students.

name: Robert Morris University FIRST Robotics Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For U.S. citizens graduating in 2027 as current FIRST participants and enrolling full-time in engineering or computer science. Minimum 3.0 GPA.

name: RIT FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For outstanding admitted first-year applicants who were on a high school FIRST team.

name: SMART Scholarship-for-Service Program
amount: Full tuition plus a $30,000-$46,000 annual stipend (portal lists $100,000)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Not FIRST-exclusive: for STEM students. Requires a 3.0 GPA, the ability to obtain a security clearance, and a post-graduation civilian service commitment. High school seniors can apply.

name: SWE Houston Area Scholarship
provider: Society of Women Engineers, Houston Area
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For high school seniors entering an ABET-accredited 4-year engineering program with a strong interest in robotics or automation and at least one FIRST competition.

name: South Dakota Mines FIRST Scholarship
provider: South Dakota School of Mines and Technology
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For seniors who took part in FRC or FTC and are admitted by the deadline. Requires an ACT of 27 or higher and a 3.5 GPA.

name: TE Connectivity FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For high school seniors on a FIRST team who plan to attend college. The portal lists a Pennsylvania location, so check eligibility.

name: Texas Tech Engineering FIRST Scholarship
provider: Texas Tech University Whitacre College of Engineering
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For incoming freshmen from an FTC or FRC team.

name: Trine University FIRST Scholarship
amount: $2,500, renewable up to $10,000 over 4 years (ten awarded)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For seniors from FRC or FTC entering the Allen School of Engineering and Computing. Requires two recommendations and an essay.

name: Tulane University FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For seniors with a full FRC or FTC season in junior or senior year who will study in the School of Science and Engineering.

name: U.S. Air Force Academy Appointment
amount: Full scholarship with room, board, and a monthly stipend (portal lists $400,000)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Not FIRST-exclusive: every cadet attends on full scholarship.

name: Grainger Engineering FIRST Scholarship
provider: University of Illinois Grainger College of Engineering
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For graduating seniors from FRC or FTC admitted to a Grainger engineering major at Urbana-Champaign.

name: UNI STEM Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For an 11th grade participant in the Iowa Regional FIRST Robotics Competition. Must apply as a junior and be accepted by UNI.

name: Valparaiso FIRST Robotics Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Selected on FIRST involvement, team accomplishments, academics, and other activities.

name: VCU FIRST Robotics Scholarship
provider: Virginia Commonwealth University College of Engineering
amount: $16,000/year, renewable up to $64,000 over 4 years (two awarded)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. Requires at least two years on a FIRST team, including senior year. FRC preferred, FTC may apply. Maintain a 3.3 GPA to renew.

name: Wentworth FIRST Robotics Scholarship
amount: $10,000/year, renewable for 4 years (up to five awarded)
deadline: January 1, 2027 (must be accepted by Early Action Round 2)
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For students who took part in FIRST Robotics consistently throughout high school.

name: Western Technical College FIRST Scholarship
notes: Listed on the FIRST Scholarship Portal. For FRC or FTC participants admitted full-time to an Integrated Technology program. Preference given to financial need.

name: Wentworth VEX Robotics Scholarship
amount: $10,000/year, renewable for 4 years (up to five awarded)
deadline: January 1 (must be accepted by Early Action Round 2)
notes: For students who took part in VEX Robotics consistently throughout high school.

name: Florida Power & Light Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Currently closed; check Scholarship America for the next cycle
notes: For seniors with at least two years in FIRST, BEST, or VEX, at a high school in FPL's Florida service area, pursuing engineering, information management, or another approved STEM program. Minimum 3.0 weighted GPA.

name: SME Education Foundation Robotics Scholarship
notes: For U.S. or Canadian undergraduates in manufacturing or industrial engineering, manufacturing technology, or a related field who competed in robotics in high school. Minimum 2.0 GPA.

name: Embry-Riddle Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For high school seniors active on any robotics team in the U.S. or its territories. Requires an essay on robotics involvement and admission to the university.

name: Illinois Tech VEX Robotics Scholarship
notes: For seniors with at least one full VEX season in junior or senior year. Any major. Requires a one-page essay.

name: Johnson & Wales Robotics Scholarship
amount: $2,500, renewable up to 4 years (no limit on awards)
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For students who competed in robotics during junior or senior year. Mention your participation in the general application.

name: MSOE Tuition Scholarship
amount: Tuition-based amount, renewable up to 6 years
notes: For freshmen, transfer, and international students from FIRST, VEX, Aerial Drone, PLTW, SkillsUSA, or TSA programs. Limit of one award.

name: Rensselaer RECF Robotics Scholarship
amount: At least $12,500/year, at least $50,000 over 4 years (up to ten awarded)
notes: For high school juniors on an RECF Robotics team. Requires a mentor or coach recommendation and an essay.

name: Syracuse Engineering VEX Scholarship
provider: Syracuse University College of Engineering and Computer Science
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For students who took part in VEX Robotics programs in high school.

name: University of Indianapolis Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: Robotics participants are automatically eligible to be considered.

name: Joanne Pransky Celebration of Women in Robotics
provider: Joanne Pransky Celebration of Women in Robotics
notes: For women and girls in robotics and drones, from high school through PhD.

name: SCTCC Robotics Full-Ride Scholarship
provider: St. Cloud Technical & Community College Foundation
notes: For a full-time student in an SCTCC STEM program with at least two years of robotics who stays active in Minnesota's robotics community. Requires an essay and a recommendation letter.

name: Florida Poly Robotics Merit Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For full-time technology and engineering students with a passion for robotics. Minimum 3.5 GPA. Competition experience preferred, not required.

name: WPI RECF Robotics and Drones Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For alumni of RECF robotics and drone programs.

name: Bryan College Robotics Team Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For students who join Bryan College's robotics team.

name: LSU Pre-Engineering Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For one outstanding freshman entering the College of Engineering.

name: Michigan State RECF Robotics Scholarship
deadline: Awarded in early April; no separate application
notes: For first-year students. List your RECF robotics participation on your MSU application.

name: UMKC Engineering Robotics Scholarships
provider: University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Science & Engineering
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: Offered to robotics participants.

name: Vaughn College VEX Scholarship
provider: Vaughn College of Aeronautics and Technology
deadline: Check current cycle on the provider's site
notes: For full-time students who competed in VEX.

name: AmericanMuscle Student Scholarship
deadline: One award each spring and fall semester
notes: For students pursuing robotics, mechanical engineering, or other automotive-themed majors.
